Subject: Initial ask — MAP and gating items for MSA/DPA/order form

Sean — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal are aligning on an accelerated path to sign; we'd like a mutual action plan that clearly calls out which items will gate signature vs which can be post-sign SOW tasks.

High-level asks from MedSpire procurement/legal:
- Clear milestone dates for MSA, DPA, and Order Form sign (our target window is Nov 20–24)
- A list of mandatory pre-sign artifacts (SOC2 evidence, org chart, insurance cert)
- Acceptance criteria that must be in the Order Form (pilot success metrics)
- Known Redwood redlines that could require senior review (data residency / indemnity)

Can you send a short MAP document and proposed schedule by EOD today? Procurement would like to kick off internal review tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Procurement — MedSpire Health
Attach: none

Aisha — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise MAP (Redwood_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) and our current MSA with suggested redlines (MSA_draft_redlines_v2.docx). Key points in the MAP:

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Nov 09: Redwood sends MAP + annotated MSA (attached) 
- Nov 10–11: MedSpire legal & procurement review + compile questions
- Nov 12: Joint sync to resolve high-impact redlines (data residency, indemnity) — internal Redwood attendees: Laura (legal), Karthik (sales ops)
- Nov 13–16: Finalize Order Form acceptance criteria and pilot acceptance tests
- Nov 17–19: Signatures routed via DocuSign (target sign window 11/20–11/24)

Pre-sign artifacts (we can provide the following immediately):
- SOC 2 Type II report (redwood.s3/secure-link)
- Insurance certificate (general liability)
- Architecture diagram + data flow (privacy-only view)

Callouts — items that typically cause escalation:
1) Data residency / geographic controls (we offer EU-only tenanting for customers; US data center default)
2) Indemnity & liability caps tied to token usage — legal often asks for clarifying language
3) SLA remedies and uptime SLOs if you need stricter terms than standard
4) Pilot acceptance criteria: we recommend page-level precision for the first 2 weeks (metrics spelled out in Order Form)

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (MAP), MSA_draft_redlines_v2.docx (annotated MSA)

If Laura or Karthik want to add redline priorities before our 11/12 sync, please flag them in reply. We can also split the Nov 12 call into a 30-minute legal-only and a 30-minute ops session.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP + redlines — internal notes

Folks — quick internal note (will not send externally until we agree):

I reviewed MSA_draft_redlines_v2.docx and annotated high-priority items we should try to resolve pre-sign:
- Data residency (Section 6): MedSpire wants EU-only for certain PHI-like workloads. We can offer a contractual commitment to US-only or EU-only tenanting but need product ops confirmation for export controls. Action: Karthik to confirm availability and any provisioning lead time.
- Indemnity (Section 11): their procurement typically pushes for broader indemnity for third-party claims. We should propose language tied to Redwood's negligence and cap it to fees paid in prior 12 months.
- SLA / Remedies (Section 8): if they request financial credits we should push for a 30-day remediation cure period before credits.
- Pilot Acceptance criteria (Order Form schedule, tab 2 in MAP): request FORMED test cases + measurement window. Procurement will likely require a signed acceptance checklist at pilot end.
- SOC2 evidence: provide redacted report and attestation summary; do not share raw logs.

I attached a redline summary for the Nov 12 meeting and flagged three clauses that need exec review if counterparty refuses our proposed language.

Attachment: MSA_redline_summary_internal.docx (internal)

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
